To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cut‐ off in the antimicrobial efficiency of N,N‐ dimethylalkylamine oxide homologues is caused by a cut‐off in their perturbing effect of bacterial membranes.
the antimicrobial activity of N,N‐ dimethylalkylamine oxide homologs correlates with their ability to perturb the structure of the bacterial membrane.
the cut‐of in the antimicrobial activity of the homologs series of N,N-dimethylalkylamine oxide is caused by the corresponding cut-off in the membrane perturbation efficiency of this series.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of structure‐activity relationships in the series of N,N ‐dimethylalkylamines.
a new approach to the study of the structure of biological membranes.
the development of new antimicrobial agents, which are based on the use of the cut‐off effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DMAOs of n = 10–14 exhibit a maximum antimicrobial activity due to their maximum perturbing effect of the bacterial membrane.
the antimicrobial activity of DMAOs is a function of the physicochemical properties, which are related to the membrane perturbation efficiency of DMAOs.

DMAOs with n > 12 have a greater potential for antimicrobial activity than DMAOs with n < 12, but the difference is only slight, and that the difference is not sufficient to explain the observed cut‐off.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cut‐offs in both antimicrobial activity and membrane perturbation efficiency of DMAO series are caused by the cut-off in their physicochemical properties.

a cut‐off effect in antimicrobial activity of homologous series is a common phenomenon and that the physicochemical properties and the effect on membrane structure are responsible for the cut‐off effect.
the cut‐ off in the antimicrobial activities of the homologues series of DMAOs is due to the cut‐off effect on the perturbing action of the DMAOs on the bacterial membrane structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the antimicrobial activity of DMAOs is determined by the physicochemical properties (critical micelle concentrations, lipid/aqueous partition coefficients, and retention times in reversed‐phase HPLC) of the homologues and the cut‐off effect in the antimicrobial activities of DMAOs is caused by the same factors that determine the cut‐off effects in the DMAO membrane perturbing activity.

the antimicrobial activity of a series of homologues is a result of their physicochemical properties and that the maximum in antimicrobial activity can be predicted based on the cut‐off effect in the membrane perturbing properties of the homologues.
the cut‐offs in the antimicrobial and in the perturbing effects on the bacterial membranes of homologous series are not necessarily identical.
